summary: In April 1850 an English traveller, newly married in Belgium, set out from Paris with his wife Emily for Constantinople by the overland road. They went through Italy to Trieste and Fiume, by carriage through Croatia and along the Austrian frontier to Semlin and Belgrade, and then on horseback with a courier, guards, and baggage horses through Servia and Ottoman Bulgaria to Nissa, Sophia, Philippopoli, and Adrianople. The book describes the roads, inns and khans, Austrian frontier officials, Turkish pachas and garrisons, the Christian villagers, gipsies, and fellow travellers, often in a joking tone.
The book was published without the author’s name. It is attributed to John Berwick Harwood, who married Emily Trollope at Ostend in April 1850.
omitted_from_reading: The line “The Bridal and the Bridle” above Chapter I is in the JSON only.
notes_on_text: The book was published anonymously. The attribution to John Berwick Harwood (1828–1899) is that of library catalogues; the book itself gives the wife’s name, Emily, and the date and place of the wedding, which agree with his marriage to Emily Trollope.
The book has no printed contents and its chapters have no titles; the places in the contents entries after each chapter number are the editor’s, spelled as the book spells them.
